nodes.text: Let $f(n)$ be the maximal number of edges in a graph on $n$ vertices such that all cycles have more vertices than chords. Is it true that $f(n)\ll n$?

#642 : [CES96] [Er97d,p.84] graph theory | cycles A problem of Hamburger and Szegedy. A chord is an edge between two vertices of the cycle which are not consecutive in the cycle. Chen, Erdős, and Staton [CES96] proved $f(n) \ll n^{3/2}$. Draganić, Methuku, Munhá Correia, and Sudakov [DMMS24] have improved this to\[f(n) \ll n(\log n)^8.\] Additional thanks to : Terence Tao and Desmond Weisenberg Proof expositions (0) If you would like to contribute an exposition of a proof related to this problem, please message a moderator or leave your exposition as a comment.
